```{r setup}
#| code-summary: "Setup: raw runs and trials, hand scores, official scores"
source(here::here("common.R"))
library(lme4)

# Raw per-site datasets, pinned to their releases of 2026-10-22 (the date of
# levante_data_latest v5_0). Raw data keep the runs production excludes,
# which for young children are many.
raw_specs <- tribble(
  ~dataset,                         ~ref,                                      ~version,
  "pilot_bostonchildrens_us_main",  "pilot_bostonchildrens_us_main_raw:7e6c",  "v7_0",
  "partner_sparklab_us_downex",     "partner_sparklab_us_downex_raw:4n9e",     "v11_0",
  "pilot_langcog_us_downex",        "pilot_langcog_us_downex_raw:a6kb",        "v13_0",
  "pilot_leuphana_de_main",         "pilot_leuphana_de_main_raw:1j0w",         "v3_0")
raw <- \(table) pmap_dfr(raw_specs, \(dataset, ref, version)
  load_levante_raw(ref, version, table) |> mutate(dataset = dataset, .before = 1))
raw_refs <- with(raw_specs, paste0(ref, ":", version))

kids <- raw("users") |>
  filter(user_type == "student") |>
  select(dataset, user_id, birth_month, birth_year)
runs <- raw("runs") |>
  inner_join(kids, by = c("dataset", "user_id")) |>
  left_join(task_lookup |> select(task_id, task_label), by = "task_id") |>
  mutate(age = (year(time_started) - birth_year) + (month(time_started) - birth_month) / 12,
         finished = !is.na(time_finished))

# official scores from the pinned release
scores_all <- load_levante_latest("scores")
data_ref <- unique(scores_all$redivis_source)
runs <- runs |>
  left_join(scores_all |> select(run_id, exclusion, score, score_se), by = "run_id") |>
  mutate(status = case_when(is.na(exclusion) & !is.na(score) ~ "scored",
                            !is.na(exclusion) ~ str_replace_all(exclusion, "_", " "),
                            run_id %in% scores_all$run_id ~ "unscored",
                            TRUE ~ "not in release"))

# test trials with simple hand-scoring rules: Hearts and Flowers responses
# count as correct only between 200 and 2,000 ms (as in production); chance
# comes from the number of response options
test <- raw("trials") |>
  filter(!is_practice_trial %in% TRUE) |>
  inner_join(runs |> select(run_id, dataset, user_id, task_label, age), by = c("run_id", "user_id", "dataset")) |>
  mutate(n_options = if_else(is.na(distractors) | distractors %in% c("", "{}"), NA_integer_,
                             str_count(distractors, ",") + 2L),
         chance = case_when(task_id == "hearts-and-flowers" ~ 0.5,
                            task_id == "memory-game" ~ 0,
                            TRUE ~ 1 / n_options),
         catch = task_id == "vocab" & corpus_trial_type %in% "catch",
         correct_hand = if_else(task_id == "hearts-and-flowers",
                                correct & !is.na(rt_numeric) & rt_numeric >= 200 & rt_numeric <= 2000,
                                correct))

run_acc <- test |>
  filter(!catch) |>
  group_by(dataset, run_id, user_id, task_id, task_label, age) |>
  summarise(trials = n(), accuracy = mean(correct_hand, na.rm = TRUE),
            chance = mean(chance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(runs |> select(run_id, status, score, score_se, finished), by = "run_id")

age_band <- \(a) cut(a, c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6.1), right = FALSE,
                     labels = c("2", "3", "4", "5"))
n_kids <- n_distinct(runs$user_id)

# children, scoring by age band, exclusions
kid_age <- runs |>
  group_by(dataset, user_id) |>
  summarise(age = min(age, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

scored_by_age <- runs |>
  mutate(band = age_band(age)) |>
  filter(!is.na(band)) |>
  group_by(band) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), share = mean(status == "scored"), .groups = "drop")

incomplete_share <- runs |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(share = mean(status == "incomplete"), .groups = "drop")

# Vocabulary catch (attention-check) trials
catch <- test |>
  filter(catch) |>
  group_by(dataset, run_id, user_id, age) |>
  summarise(pass = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
catch_by_band <- catch |>
  mutate(band = age_band(age)) |>
  group_by(band) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), pass = mean(pass), .groups = "drop")

# accuracy change with age under 3.5
liftoff <- test |>
  filter(!catch, age < 3.5, !is.na(correct_hand)) |>
  group_by(task_label) |>
  filter(n_distinct(user_id) >= 8) |>
  group_modify(\(d, key) {
    m <- glmer(correct_hand ~ age + (1 | user_id), data = d, family = binomial,
               control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
    est <- fixef(m)[["age"]]; se <- sqrt(vcov(m)["age", "age"])
    tibble(children = n_distinct(d$user_id), trials = nrow(d), slope = est,
           lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(slope)

# official scores against hand-scored accuracy
score_vs_hand <- run_acc |>
  filter(status == "scored") |>
  group_by(dataset, task_label) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  reframe(cor_ci(score, accuracy))

# the same, standardized within dataset and task and pooled per dataset,
# so datasets with few runs per task can be compared
score_vs_hand_ds <- run_acc |>
  filter(status == "scored") |>
  group_by(dataset, task_label) |>
  filter(n() >= 5) |>
  mutate(score_z = as.numeric(scale(score)), acc_z = as.numeric(scale(accuracy))) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  reframe(cor_ci(score_z, acc_z))
lost_age2 <- runs |>
  filter(age_band(age) == "2", status != "scored") |>
  count(status, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(runs$age >= 2 & runs$age < 3, na.rm = TRUE))

# official scores by age: English-speaking school-age children (Canada, UK)
# as a reference band, by half-year of age
reference_ds <- c("pilot_western_ca_main", "rfp1_sheffield_gb_main")
reference <- scores_all |>
  filter(dataset %in% reference_ds, is.na(exclusion), !is.na(score), age < 9) |>
  left_join(task_lookup |> select(task_id, task_label), by = "task_id") |>
  filter(task_label %in% run_acc$task_label) |>
  mutate(age = floor(age * 2) / 2 + 0.25) |>
  group_by(task_label, age) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(median = median(score), q25 = quantile(score, .25),
            q75 = quantile(score, .75), .groups = "drop")
score_age <- run_acc |>
  filter(status == "scored", !is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(task_label) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  reframe(cor_ci(score, age))

# Sparklab's repeat runs
sparklab_repeats <- runs |>
  filter(dataset == "partner_sparklab_us_downex") |>
  arrange(user_id, time_started) |>
  group_by(user_id) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), span_days = as.numeric(difftime(max(time_started),
                                                        min(time_started), units = "days")),
            .groups = "drop")

# LangCog checks
lc_runs <- runs |> filter(dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex")
lc_trials_v5 <- load_levante_latest("trials") |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex")
items <- load_levante_latest("items")
lc_test <- test |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex") |>
  count(run_id, name = "test_trials")
lc_incomplete <- lc_runs |>
  filter(status == "incomplete") |>
  left_join(lc_test, by = "run_id")
complete_trials <- test |>
  semi_join(runs |> filter(finished), by = "run_id") |>
  count(task_label, run_id) |>
  group_by(task_label) |>
  summarise(median_complete = median(n), .groups = "drop")

langcog <- tibble(
  runs = nrow(lc_runs), children = n_distinct(lc_runs$user_id),
  first = min(as.Date(lc_runs$time_started)), last = max(as.Date(lc_runs$time_started)),
  versions = paste(sort(unique(sub("-.*", "", lc_runs$task_version))), collapse = ", "),
  share_scored = mean(lc_runs$status == "scored"),
  share_incomplete = mean(lc_runs$status == "incomplete"),
  incomplete_unfinished = mean(!lc_incomplete$finished),
  incomplete_at_complete_length = sum(lc_incomplete |>
    left_join(complete_trials, by = "task_label") |>
    with(test_trials >= median_complete), na.rm = TRUE),
  in_bank = mean(lc_trials_v5$item_uid %in% items$item_uid))
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Summary

**Data:** the four raw datasets, pinned to their releases of 2026-10-22
(see Notes), for runs and trials; `r data_ref` for official scores.

- `r fmt_n(n_kids)` children aged
  `r round(min(runs$age, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`–`r round(max(runs$age, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`
  ran `r fmt_n(nrow(runs))` tasks across the four datasets.
  `r fmt_n(sum(kid_age$age < 3))` of them were under 3, all in
  `r paste(unique(dataset_labels_named[kid_age$dataset[kid_age$age < 3]]), collapse = ", ")`;
  Leuphana's `r sum(kid_age$dataset == "pilot_leuphana_de_main")` children
  were `r paste(round(range(kid_age$age[kid_age$dataset == "pilot_leuphana_de_main"]), 1), collapse = "–")`.
- Production scores `r fmt_pct(mean(runs$status == "scored"))` of these runs,
  falling from `r fmt_pct(pick(scored_by_age, share, band == "5"))` at age 5 to
  `r fmt_pct(pick(scored_by_age, share, band == "2"))` at age 2. Most of the
  two-year-olds' lost runs have
  `r lost_age2$status[1]` (`r fmt_pct(lost_age2$share[1])` of their runs) or
  `r lost_age2$status[2]` (`r fmt_pct(lost_age2$share[2])`).
- Under age 3.5, accuracy rises with age on
  `r paste(liftoff$task_label[liftoff$lo > 0], collapse = ", ")`; it shows no
  reliable rise on `r paste(liftoff$task_label[liftoff$lo <= 0], collapse = ", ")`.
- Official scores rise with age in `r sum(score_age$lo > 0)` of the
  `r nrow(score_age)` tasks with 20 or more scored runs, and track
  hand-scored accuracy: r =
  `r f2(min(score_vs_hand$r))`–`r f2(max(score_vs_hand$r))` in each dataset
  and task with 20 or more scored runs.
- LangCog's runs, from early beta versions of the tasks, need no rescoring:
  their scored runs map to calibrated items and track accuracy as closely as
  the other datasets' (r =
  `r f2(pick(score_vs_hand_ds, r, dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex"))`
  within task, against
  `r paste(f2(score_vs_hand_ds$r[score_vs_hand_ds$dataset != "pilot_langcog_us_downex"]), collapse = " and ")`). `r fmt_pct(langcog$share_incomplete)` of them are excluded
  as incomplete, against
  `r fmt_pct(max(incomplete_share$share[incomplete_share$dataset != "pilot_langcog_us_downex"]))`
  or less elsewhere, and these runs are genuinely unfinished.
:::

# Who and what

```{r children, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-children
#| fig-cap: "Children by age at their first run, by dataset."
kid_age |>
  mutate(dataset_label = dataset_labels_named[dataset]) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 2, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_dataset(name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:6) +
  labs(x = "Age at first run (years)", y = "Children") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r coverage, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Runs of each task in each dataset."
runs |>
  count(dataset, task_label, name = "runs") |>
  mutate(dataset_label = factor(dataset_labels_named[dataset],
                                rev(dataset_labels_named[raw_specs$dataset]))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = task_label, y = dataset_label, fill = runs)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = runs, colour = runs > 100), size = 3.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
```

Sparklab ran Math only, and it is not longitudinal:
`r fmt_n(sum(sparklab_repeats$runs == 1))` of its
`r fmt_n(nrow(sparklab_repeats))` children have a single run, and repeat
runs are mostly re-administrations in the same session (median
`r round(median(sparklab_repeats$span_days[sparklab_repeats$runs > 1]) * 24 * 60)`
minutes between a child's first and last run; longest
`r round(max(sparklab_repeats$span_days))` days).

## What production scores

```{r status, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-status
#| fig-cap: "What production did with each run, by age."
runs |>
  mutate(band = age_band(age)) |>
  filter(!is.na(band)) |>
  count(band, status) |>
  group_by(band) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(status = fct_relevel(status, "scored")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share, y = fct_rev(band), fill = status)) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Share of runs", y = "Age (years)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Accuracy by age

Each point is one run; lines are smooths within each dataset with 20 or
more runs of the task. The dashed line is chance. Vocabulary's attention-check (catch) trials are left
out.

```{r accuracy, fig.height=7.5}
#| label: fig-accuracy
#| fig-cap: "Hand-scored accuracy by age, one point per run, with a smooth for each dataset with 20 or more runs of the task. Dashed line: chance."
chance_lines <- run_acc |>
  group_by(task_label) |>
  summarise(chance = mean(chance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(chance > 0)

ggplot(run_acc, aes(x = age, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_hline(data = chance_lines, aes(yintercept = chance), lty = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = dataset), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(data = run_acc |> group_by(dataset, task_label) |> filter(n() >= 20),
              aes(colour = dataset), method = "loess", span = 1, se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(vars(task_label)) +
  scale_colour_dataset(name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Proportion correct (hand-scored)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r catch, fig.height=3.5}
#| label: fig-catch
#| fig-cap: "Vocabulary catch trials passed, by age."
ggplot(catch, aes(x = age, y = pass)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = dataset), width = 0, height = 0.02, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 1, se = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.25, lty = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_dataset(name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:6) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Catch trials passed") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Vocabulary's catch trials are easy items that check the child is engaged.
Two-year-olds pass `r fmt_pct(pick(catch_by_band, pass, band == "2"))` of
them (`r pick(catch_by_band, runs, band == "2")` runs), against
`r fmt_pct(pick(catch_by_band, pass, band == "3"))` at age 3.

# Which tasks work under 3.5

For children under 3.5, the change in the log odds of a correct answer per
year of age, from a logistic model with a random intercept for each child
(tasks with 8 or more such children; 95% CIs). A reliably positive slope
means accuracy rises with age within the band, so the task measures
something there.

```{r liftoff, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-liftoff
#| fig-cap: "Change in the log odds of a correct answer per year of age, for children under 3.5 (95% CIs)."
liftoff |>
  mutate(task_label = factor(task_label, task_label),
         label = glue("{children} children")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = slope, y = task_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = label), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Change in log odds correct per year of age, under 3.5", y = NULL)
```

```{r young-accuracy, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-young-accuracy
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy above chance by half-year of age, under 4."
young <- run_acc |>
  filter(age < 4, task_label %in% liftoff$task_label, chance > 0) |>
  mutate(band = cut(age, c(2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4), right = FALSE,
                    labels = c("2–2.5", "2.5–3", "3–3.5", "3.5–4"))) |>
  group_by(task_label, band) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), accuracy = mean(accuracy), chance = mean(chance),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(young, aes(x = band, y = accuracy - chance, group = task_label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(size = runs)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(task_label)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3.5, name = "Runs") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Accuracy above chance")

hf_young <- test |>
  filter(task_id == "hearts-and-flowers", age < 3) |>
  summarise(raw = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE), windowed = mean(correct_hand, na.rm = TRUE),
            slow = mean(rt_numeric > 2000, na.rm = TRUE))
```

At 2–2.5, accuracy is at or below chance (no more than .05 above it) on
`r paste(young$task_label[young$band == "2–2.5" & young$accuracy - young$chance <= .05], collapse = ", ")`.
Hearts and Flowers falls below chance for children under 3 because
`r fmt_pct(hf_young$slow)` of their responses are slower than 2 seconds and
count as wrong: their accuracy is `r f2(hf_young$raw)` before the
response-time window and `r f2(hf_young$windowed)` after it.

# Official scores

Production scores these children with the item parameters calibrated on
5–12-year-olds, so their scores sit on the same scale as the school-age
children's (@fig-official-by-age).

```{r official-by-age, fig.height=7.5}
#| label: fig-official-by-age
#| fig-cap: "Official scores by age for children under 6 (points, by dataset). Grey: the median and middle half of English-speaking school-age children's scores (Canada and the UK) at each half-year of age."
ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = reference, aes(x = age, ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
              fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(data = reference, aes(x = age, y = median), colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(data = run_acc |> filter(status == "scored"),
             aes(x = age, y = score, colour = dataset), alpha = 0.5, size = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(task_label), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_dataset(name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:9) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Official score") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Among the children under 6, scores correlate with age at r =
`r f2(min(score_age$r))`–`r f2(max(score_age$r))` across tasks, and the
95% CI excludes zero for
`r paste(score_age$task_label[score_age$lo > 0], collapse = ", ")`.

For runs it scored, the correlation of the official score with hand-scored
accuracy, by dataset and task (20 or more scored runs):

```{r score-vs-hand, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-score-vs-hand
#| fig-cap: "Correlation of official scores with hand-scored accuracy, by dataset and task (95% CIs)."
score_vs_hand |>
  mutate(task_label = reorder(task_label, r)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = r, y = task_label, colour = dataset)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_colour_dataset(name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Correlation of official score with hand-scored accuracy (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r score-se, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-score-se
#| fig-cap: "Standard errors of the official scores, by age."
run_acc |>
  filter(status == "scored", !is.na(score_se)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = score_se)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = dataset), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 1, se = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(vars(task_label)) +
  scale_colour_dataset(name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Standard error of the official score") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Median standard errors are
`r f2(median(run_acc$score_se[run_acc$status == "scored" & run_acc$age < 4], na.rm = TRUE))`
under age 4 and
`r f2(median(run_acc$score_se[run_acc$status == "scored" & run_acc$age >= 5], na.rm = TRUE))`
at age 5 and over.

# LangCog's older runs

LangCog collected `r langcog$runs` runs from `r langcog$children` children
between `r format(langcog$first, "%B %Y")` and
`r format(langcog$last, "%B %Y")`, on early versions of the tasks (mostly
1.0.0 betas). Three checks:

- **Item identity.** The raw beta trials carry no item identifiers, but
  processing reconstructs them: `r fmt_pct(langcog$in_bank, 1)` of
  LangCog's processed trials map to calibrated items.
- **Scores.** LangCog has too few scored runs per task for the figure
  above, so scores and accuracy are standardized within each task with 5 or
  more scored runs and correlated across tasks: r =
  `r f2(pick(score_vs_hand_ds, r, dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex"))`
  (95% CI
  `r f2(pick(score_vs_hand_ds, lo, dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex"))` to
  `r f2(pick(score_vs_hand_ds, hi, dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex"))`,
  `r pick(score_vs_hand_ds, n, dataset == "pilot_langcog_us_downex")` runs),
  in line with Boston and Sparklab.
- **Exclusions.** Production scores `r fmt_pct(langcog$share_scored)` of
  LangCog's runs and excludes `r fmt_pct(langcog$share_incomplete)` as
  incomplete. `r fmt_pct(langcog$incomplete_unfinished)` of those have no
  finish time, and only `r langcog$incomplete_at_complete_length` reached the
  median length of a finished run of the same task, so they are unfinished
  runs rather than finished runs that were not marked complete.

So LangCog's runs need no rescoring. Whether runs that young children don't
finish should be scored is a question for the whole age band.

# Notes

- **Raw versions.** Each raw dataset is pinned to its release of
  2026-10-22, the date of the pinned `levante_data_latest` release, so runs
  and official scores line up:
  `r paste0("\x60", raw_refs, "\x60", collapse = ", ")`.
- **Ages** come from birth month and year and each run's start time, so they
  are accurate to about a month.
- **Hand scoring** is the proportion of test trials correct, with the
  Hearts and Flowers response-time window applied as in production. Same and
  Different and Memory count trials differently from the dashboard, so their
  accuracies are only comparable within the task.

# Revision history

- **2026-10-30.** Rewritten on pinned data and widened from Boston
  Children's alone to all four datasets with children under 6 (Boston,
  Sparklab, LangCog, Leuphana), with official scores from the pinned release
  and a check of LangCog's early-version runs. The item-level vocabulary
  analysis, the CAT running-θ section and the per-task hand scores of the
  earlier page ("10 — Downward extension (Boston Children's, ages 2–5)") are
  not carried over; it is in `archive/`.
